links.outcome: User control over personal data and ability to disable data sharing in AI healthcare chatbot apps
links.effect: Only two of 12 apps offered an option to disable data sharing at sign-up; users had minimal control over their personal data.
links.quote: Moreover, users had minimal control over their personal data.

links.outcome: Whether apps informed users of data use through a privacy policy at sign-up
links.effect: Half of the 12 apps did not present a privacy policy during sign-up; most policies failed to address data protection measures.
links.quote: Our findings reveal that half of the examined apps did not present a privacy policy during sign up, and only two provided an option to disable data sharing at that stage.

screen.reason: Empirical audit/assessment of real-world consumer AI healthcare chatbot apps evaluating their privacy practices, policies, and controls, but does not test or compare a specific deployment practice/safeguard intervention.
